name: Academic CPU Insight
purpose: Editable Chinese scientific-technical leadership slides on mobile AArch64 CPU, LLVM, heterogeneous SoCs and evidence-constrained 2027–2029 Agentic AI.

style.visual_language: Chinese academic technical decision presentation: blue monochrome hierarchy, precise CPU/ISA and CPU-NPU schematics, source-labelled plots, visible uncertainty, clear directed edges, restrained line icons and native PowerPoint shapes. Do not invent CPU modules, measurements, comparisons or hardware commitments.
style.whitespace: Evidence rich with systematic title, diagram and citation spacing. Never create empty decoration or tiny labels solely to fill a template.

rules: Navy and a single blue family carry authored hierarchy; use whites and cold greys for neutral fields.
Do not use orange or unrelated accent palettes for slides; warning states use text, outline and labels rather than an unlabelled color.
Information state must not be encoded solely by color. Pair color with label or line treatment.
Text remains high contrast; diagrams and citations must be readable on a projector.
Use a Chinese-capable sans font for all text roles; verify local availability and Office substitutions before final release.
One shared conclusion-title role across content slides; prefer native PowerPoint text, not texture-baked generated words.
Source labels and device/baseline limitations must remain legible.
Use solid blue and cold-grey native chart series; no decorative gradients in quantitative plots.
Include model, device, baseline and statistic scope for each source-derived data number.
Never combine incompatible devices, models, environments or relative denominators into a common rank chart.

icons.asset_policy: Use neutral line Remix Icon or MDI assets of coherent stroke weight. Do not use consulting-branded orange icons or unsupported unofficial processor logos.
avoid: mixed filled and outlined icon glyphs in one peer group

geometry: Align related elements on an intentional grid; never treat arrow endpoints as approximate.
SME/SME2 is a CPU ISA feature and must be inside the CPU core hierarchy when depicted.
DAG and tool-execution arrows have explicit source, target and relation type.
Keep a clear source/citation area and do not let reference lines collide with content.
composition: Use an explanatory main visual, not generic equal cards by default.
Conclusion title must be readable without knowing project notation.
Separate priority engineering tracks from conditional research reserves and unsupported new silicon bets.
Labels for assumptions and limitations are substantive content, not optional decoration.
reconstruction: Native PowerPoint text, shapes, chart objects and connectors take priority.
Inherited master header/footer and slide numbers are outside generated substantive content.
Use the packaged SlidePoise semantic-map, OpenCV measurement and reconstruction workflow; do not paste one full-slide image.
Review actual PowerPoint rendering, not just code or source SVG.

reasoning_principles: Start from the audience question and the one belief, understanding, or decision the slide should create.
Treat the slide as an argument unit, not a container for topics.
Distinguish claim, evidence, context, qualification, and recommendation when those roles exist.
Preserve sequence, comparison, hierarchy, causality, dependency, contribution, and parallelism when supported by the content.
Do not invent completeness, causality, or evidence that the source material does not support.
Use MECE only as a diagnostic when the content is intended to be a complete decomposition.
visual_principles: Use one disciplined blue science/engineering visual system across slides; vary diagram layouts by explanatory job.
Explicitly show control-flow, data-flow and conditional arrows with legend and direction.
Put quantitative evidence on the same page as its device, baseline and evaluation boundary.
Prefer native directed DAGs, CPU nested architecture schematics, small multiples and roadmap matrices to decorative hardware imagery.
Information dense but readable for technical leadership without deep Agent background.
writing_principles: Write Chinese conclusion-led slide titles, not questions or one-word topics.
Introduce specialized terms before relying on them, and keep research-internal codes in speaker notes.
Discuss source boundaries and counterpressure when they change the decision.
review_questions: Can a technical leader state the takeaway and evidence from this slide alone?
Are AArch64/SME2/CPU/NPU/Runtime shown in correct levels?
Do experimental devices, units, statistics and baselines match evidence cards?
Is the slide's blue palette consistent with all resolved native objects, icon colors, text policies, charts and master frame?
Does every arrow connect the correct source and destination and have an explainable meaning?
Are all substantial PowerPoint objects native and editable where reasonable?
Are source limitations and unsupported claims visible and preserved in speaker notes?
anti_patterns: orange/Georgia leftovers from the source Consulting profile
no-name CPU/NPU acceleration numbers or invented bar-chart data
SME as standalone compute engine next to CPU
substituting generic accelerator/PIM/storage topics for the formally approved three conditional research questions
arrows overlapping or connecting the wrong objects
entire-slide raster PNG passed as editable PowerPoint
